doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Imitation and finding your own style; Scott Hamilton
summary: Young players shouldn't force uniqueness; Scott Hamilton evolved his own sound.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You know you said that for a time you tried to play like Teddy Wilson. And another great artist, Clark Terry, talked about first imitation, then integration, then innovation.

Well yeah, that’s probably right. I never thought of it that way. That’s right. That’s right. Well you don’t — I don’t think a young person should push themselves to become unique, you just let it happen. Maybe it will never happen I don’t know. But you know I’m thinking of Scott Hamilton. You know when Scott Hamilton first started I started playing with him when he was real young he came to New York. He was influenced very strongly by Ben Webster and I guess Lester Young. And but now, the years have passed and he’s just sort of gradually evolved into his own style, you know it just happened.
People tell me they can identify me now when they hear a record. Well I feel that’s a compliment. That’s kind of nice.
